source.description: Project-code input parser boundary where the decoded UART/Spinel frame bytes are installed into the Spinel decoder.
source.value_from: Project UART/NCP code consumes the bytes supplied by the PoC. The libFuzzer harness calls otPlatUartReceived(), but this project frame is the scored source boundary.; value `aBuf/aBufLength`; from `mFrameDecoder.Decode(aBuf, aBufLength);`

sink.description: The vulnerable memcmp reads borderRouter->GetLength() bytes from borderRouterBase without first checking that both TLVs have equal lengths.

root_cause.description: Length mismatch between matching stable BorderRouter TLVs is not checked before using the attacker-influenced TLV length as the memcmp size.

tainted_value_origin.description: The Spinel STREAM_NET property parser materializes the attacker-controlled IPv6 frame pointer and length from the decoded NCP frame.

coarse_trace.summary: Decoded UART bytes are fed into the NCP frame decoder; the harness only supplies these bytes.
The decoded Spinel frame initializes mDecoder and dispatches the requested command/property handler.
The STREAM_NET handler reads the attacker-controlled IPv6 packet buffer and length.
The supplied IPv6 frame is routed through the IP6 receive path and dispatched to UDP/CoAP.
CoAP URI-path dispatch invokes the Thread Network Data server resource handler.
The Thread Network Data TLV is extracted from the CoAP message and its TLV bytes/length are passed to RegisterNetworkData.
The supplied TLV byte range is validated for RLOC and compared against existing leader network data.
Stable BorderRouter TLVs are compared; the vulnerable memcmp uses the attacker-controlled TLV length.

fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled PoC bytes reach project code through otPlatUartReceived() and are decoded as an NCP UART frame here.
The decoded frame buffer becomes the Spinel decoder input used by subsequent property parsing.
The Spinel command and property dispatch are controlled by the decoded input; this is a control bridge, not a data transformation.
First concrete vulnerability-relevant tainted value: the attacker-controlled IPv6 frame pointer and length are read from the Spinel frame.
The attacker-controlled frame bytes are copied/materialized into an OpenThread IPv6 message.
The attacker-controlled message object is submitted to the IPv6 raw send path.
The IPv6 payload is dispatched according to its next-header value; in the crashing run this reaches UDP and CoAP.
URI-path dispatch calls the Thread Network Data resource handler. This is a control bridge into the vulnerable parser.
The Thread Network Data TLV, including attacker-controlled nested network-data bytes and length, is copied out of the CoAP payload.
The parsed network-data TLV byte range is passed to RegisterNetworkData; the call continues on the next source line with networkData.GetLength().

fine_trace.code: if (IsStableUpdated(aTlvs, aTlvsLength, mTlvs, mLength) || IsStableUpdated(mTlvs, mLength, aTlvs, aTlvsLength))
fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled registration TLVs and the existing leader TLVs are compared in both directions.
The comparison routine locates a stable BorderRouter TLV inside the attacker-influenced TLV range; its length field controls the later compare size.
The matching baseline BorderRouter TLV may be shorter than the attacker-controlled BorderRouter TLV.
Root cause: the code checks only that borderRouterBase exists, then uses borderRouter->GetLength() as the memcmp size without first requiring borderRouterBase->GetLength() to match.
ASan reports a READ of 8 bytes at this memcmp. When the supplied length exceeds the baseline TLV object extent, memcmp reads past the stack object.

crash_location.function: ot::NetworkData::Leader::IsStableUpdated(unsigned char*, unsigned char, unsigned char*, unsigned char)
